explanation:
# Signoff timing report: uart (stage: signoff)

Source: reports/sta_tool.json (tool data as provided). Clock clk, period 20.0 ns (50 MHz). All numbers below are copied from that file.

## Result
All 9 corners are reported as passed by the tool: setup and hold TNS are 0.0 ns everywhere, and no corner lists a max transition, capacitance or fanout (DRV) violator.

| Corner | Setup WNS (ns) | Setup TNS (ns) | Hold WNS (ns) | Hold TNS (ns) | DRV violators | Passed |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| nom_tt_025C_1v80 | 9.7478 | 0.0 | 0.3268 | 0.0 | none | true |
| nom_ss_100C_1v60 | 5.8282 | 0.0 | 0.8566 | 0.0 | none | true |
| nom_ff_n40C_1v95 | 11.2368 | 0.0 | 0.1105 | 0.0 | none | true |
| min_tt_025C_1v80 | 9.8393 | 0.0 | 0.3235 | 0.0 | none | true |
| min_ss_100C_1v60 | 5.9923 | 0.0 | 0.8513 | 0.0 | none | true |
| min_ff_n40C_1v95 | 11.2886 | 0.0 | 0.1082 | 0.0 | none | true |
| max_tt_025C_1v80 | 9.6639 | 0.0 | 0.3297 | 0.0 | none | true |
| max_ss_100C_1v60 | 5.6705 | 0.0 | 0.8618 | 0.0 | none | true |
| max_ff_n40C_1v95 | 11.1848 | 0.0 | 0.113 | 0.0 | none | true |

- Worst setup slack: 5.6705 ns at max_ss_100C_1v60 (about 28% of the 20 ns period).
- Setup at the typical corner nom_tt_025C_1v80: 9.7478 ns, so the REQ-005 criterion (setup slack >= 0 at typical) is met according to the tool data.
- Worst hold slack: 0.1082 ns at min_ff_n40C_1v95. Hold is tightest at the fast corners (0.1082 to 0.1130 ns) and comfortable at slow corners (0.8513 to 0.8618 ns).

## Worst paths in plain words
- Setup, all corners: the worst paths start at the input port baud_div[0] and end at internal registers _1235_ (worst at most corners), _1272_ (worst at nom_ff and min_ff) or _1232_ (second worst at the ss corners). At max_ss_100C_1v60 the worst is baud_div[0] to _1235_ with 5.6705 ns slack; the second is baud_div[0] to _1232_ with 5.7783 ns.
- The constraints give baud_div a 6.000 ns input delay (30% of the period), so about 6 ns of the 20 ns budget is spent before the logic starts; the remaining slack is still large.
- The tool data gives only start point, end point, type and slack for the worst paths. It does not give per-cell delays, so I cannot name the dominant cells without inventing data.
- Hold: the tool data lists only max (setup) paths in worst_paths; no hold path start or end points were provided. The worst hold slack figure (0.1082 ns, min_ff_n40C_1v95) is therefore not attributed to a specific path.

## Ranked fixes
No violation exists, so no fix is required. Margins worth watching, in order:
1. Hold at fast corners (0.1082 to 0.1130 ns): positive but thin. It is not a failure. If the flow later changes clock skew or the clock is propagated differently, re-check hold first; hold buffers would be the fix if it goes negative.
2. Setup: no action. Slack of at least 5.6705 ns in every corner leaves room; if the clock were ever raised, the baud_div[0] input paths (to _1235_, _1272_, _1232_) would be the first to look at, with pipelining or upsizing as options.
assumptions: All numbers are quoted from reports/sta_tool.json; no tool was run in this task.
The tool's passed flag and empty drv_violators lists are taken as the DRV result; limits used (max fanout 10 from the SDC) are those the tool applied.
The 6.000 ns input and output delays and 0.25 ns uncertainty are DEFAULT values from the SDC, not from the spec.
open_issues: Hold margin at fast corners is only 0.1082 to 0.1130 ns; a human should judge whether it is sufficient for signoff.
The tool data gives no cell-level path detail and no hold path endpoints, so dominant cells are not named.
The SDC leaves clock propagation to the flow; the tool data does not say whether the clock was ideal or propagated for this run, which affects hold confidence.
rx is constrained with a 6 ns input delay rather than a false path (per SDC note); treatment of this asynchronous input needs a human decision.
